_note: The media. Every outlet works on its audience every month: it pulls their views toward its slant ('pos', only the issues it cares about, -100..100 like the axes), warms them to the party it favours, and shields that party (its audience forgives its unpopular statements). 'honesty' 0..1: honest outlets reach widely, move each viewer a little and report what you actually do; partisan ones move and shield their own audience much more and favour whoever is closest to their slant. 'reach': base share of a group that follows it, times 'by' (age, class, region, nationality multipliers). 'tones': how each way of speaking plays there (1 = neutral). 'kind': public, paper, tabloid, business, network, online, regional, platform, foreign. 'price': millions of pezo to buy it (0 = not for sale). Drafts: rename and retune freely. Foreign outlets name their 'country'. Personalities (kind 'influencer') can be sponsored: 'sponsor' is the price per quarter in millions; a sponsored personality backs the party paying, but is believed less, and the deal can come out. FOREIGN_MONEY: what comes with the secret foreign offers in content.json (FUNDING_OFFERS, by 'offer' id) once you take one: 'quarterly' millions more every quarter, the country's channel ('country', if it has one) on your side, free bot farms on social media, and favours asked now and then ('demands', each with a 'comply' answer and its effects; refusing ends the money). It ends when the offer's leak event comes out.

OUTLETS.name: CBC
OUTLETS.blurb: The national broadcaster. Bound to be balanced, and mostly is.

OUTLETS.name: The Cranebo Herald
OUTLETS.owner: the Vandel family, publishers for four generations
OUTLETS.blurb: The broadsheet of the capital. Reads like a university, prices like a bank.

OUTLETS.name: The Morning Post
OUTLETS.owner: Henrik Strell, who also owns half the country's billboards
OUTLETS.blurb: The biggest-selling paper in the country. Three words to a headline.

OUTLETS.name: The Pezo Ledger
OUTLETS.owner: a consortium of the country's banks
OUTLETS.blurb: Read on every trading floor. Thinks every problem is a tax.

OUTLETS.name: Eagle TV
OUTLETS.owner: Henrik Strell again, through a company in James
OUTLETS.blurb: Twenty-four hours of outrage, mostly about Cranebo.

OUTLETS.name: The Kettle
OUTLETS.owner: its readers, and a retired union boss who pays the deficit
OUTLETS.blurb: Started as a union newsletter. Now the left's loudest channel.

OUTLETS.name: The regional Couriers
OUTLETS.owner: a chain of local papers bought up one at a time
OUTLETS.blurb: One in every province. They cover the council, the harvest and whoever came to town.

OUTLETS.name: Clipr
OUTLETS.owner: a tech company nobody can find an address for
OUTLETS.blurb: Thirty-second videos. The algorithm loves a fight.

OUTLETS.name: Chatter
OUTLETS.owner: a billionaire who posts on it at three in the morning
OUTLETS.blurb: Where journalists and politicians shout at each other in public.

OUTLETS.name: Trueants International
OUTLETS.blurb: Broadcast across the border in Alinni. Says the Alinni are mistreated, which is sometimes true.

OUTLETS.name: Dillihan World
OUTLETS.owner: the Dillihan state, at arm's length
OUTLETS.blurb: Polished, well funded and quietly on Dillihan's side.

OUTLETS.name: Lena Vos
OUTLETS.owner: herself, and a few thousand monthly supporters
OUTLETS.blurb: Explains the economy in ten minutes with a whiteboard. Her viewers think the rest of the media is lying.

OUTLETS.name: Jory Bakk
OUTLETS.owner: himself, from a farm outside Kansilia
OUTLETS.blurb: Films himself on a tractor, talking about Cranebo. Two million views a week.

OUTLETS.name: Marek Dunn
OUTLETS.blurb: A four-hour podcast about how everything is rigged. Sells vitamins in the breaks.

OUTLETS.name: Pim
OUTLETS.owner: himself, and a sponsor who makes energy drinks
OUTLETS.blurb: Streams games eight hours a day to a quarter of the country's teenagers. Has never mentioned politics.

OUTLETS.name: Dalia Ross
OUTLETS.owner: herself; her lawyers are kept busy
OUTLETS.blurb: Celebrity gossip and online feuds. If two famous people fall out, she had it first.

OUTLETS.name: Kova Teller
OUTLETS.owner: himself; formerly of the Pezo Ledger
OUTLETS.blurb: An economist with charts on Chatter. Bankers read him; so do people who want to sound like bankers.

OUTLETS.name: Nina from Nikecisa
OUTLETS.owner: herself, and the brands she wears
OUTLETS.blurb: Cafés, harbour sunsets and opinions about the trams. Everyone in Yamlin under forty follows her.

demands.title: A quiet word from Dillihan
demands.text: Your friends at the Dillihan energy company would like the party to say less about the Fauran border for a while. Nothing public; just less.

demands.title: A ports bill they care about
demands.text: Dillihan wants Cranebonistan's ports opened to its shipping firms. Your friends ask the party to back the bill.

demands.title: The intermediaries ask about Alinni
demands.text: The Trueant intermediaries would like the party to call for Alinni-language schools. Good for the Alinni, they say, and good for the friendship.

demands.title: A softer word on the border
demands.text: There are troops on both sides of the Trueant border. The intermediaries hope the party will call for calm rather than for more troops.

demands.title: About the James mines
demands.text: The Potanian mining company thinks Cranebonian firms have had the James concessions too long, and would like the party to call for an open tender.

demands.title: The Golban lobby has a tariff in mind
demands.text: The Golban trade lobby would like the party to oppose any tariff on Golban goods, whatever happens to the pezo.
